title: Gatekeeper TTFT retune — POC sync
topics: Streaming handshake and early token hedging
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on TTFT regressions after enabling 4-bit quant and a new kernel path. Action owners assigned; Redwood to share updated bench sheets and small script for local profiling.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 51 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood SRE); Jordan Lee (HelioWorks), Priya Narayanan (HelioWorks Infra), Marco Diaz (HelioWorks PM)

Summary (auto-generated): team focused on TTFT regressions after enabling the 4-bit quant path; discussed streaming handshake timings and kernel selection for long sequences.

[00:00] Ava: ok hey everyone thanks for squeezing this in, um Jordan, you able to share the latest microburst graph so we can align?
[00:18] Jordan: yeah sure, i'm pulling it now, the main thing we saw was TTFT creeping from ~45ms to 78ms after the quant flip, but average token time downstream stayed ok, so it's like initial handshake or kernel warmup, maybe kv cache warming, not sure
[00:37] Samir: got it, thanks. quick question, do we have the same profile with streaming on and off? i remember when streaming is enabled the handshake path can add a couple tens of ms if the first chunk is small
[00:51] Jordan: we toggled streaming, seems slightly better for longer prompts but worse for short questions. weird.
[01:06] Priya: and fyi our infra team reported a spike in TCP retransmits during the morning window, could be network microbursts, not pure model perf
[01:20] Maya: that matches the traces we captured on the VPC side — small spikes at 10-40ms intervals, aligns with our burst window config, might amplify TTFT
[01:33] Ava: ok so two likely culprits: kernel/quant warmup + network microbursting. actionably we can try a kernel fallback for first token or a relaxed quant path. Samir, do you want to talk through kernel choices?
[01:47] Samir: sure. so currently the canary is running the new int4-optimized kernel which reduces GPU memory but increases kernel launch overhead for small sequences. for seq<128 it's fine, but when we hit seq around 512-2048 the kernel dispatch pattern causes extra setup. there is an alternate kernel route that does a light-weight fastpath for the first few tokens, we call it the "gatekeeper" path internally — it's less quant-aggressive and pays some memory for lower latency
[02:14] Marco: when you say pay memory, do you mean we need bigger instance sizes? we have capacity constraints on Dedicated for now
[02:24] Samir: small bump, should fit within your existing reserved pool but we'd recommend a short canary to validate. It's a per-request routing change not a cluster resize usually
[02:36] Jordan: what about prefix caching? could we keep shorter KV prefix in RAM to avoid warmup? we do a lot of 2-4 prompt turns
[02:48] Maya: prefix caching helps but if the first token path hits the quant conversion we still see overhead. we can try a hybrid: small prefix cached and gatekeeper first-token fastpath until we confirm KV hit rate improves
[03:02] Priya: also curious if batching is making it worse in your tests, we often see small bursts followed by idle which cause odd batching behavior
[03:12] Samir: good point. our autoscaler deliberately uses microbatching to reduce latency at the cost of throughput in low QPS windows; those microbatches can add jitter to TTFT. we'll check batch thresholds.
[03:26] Ava: ok let's walk through the microburst trace, jordan?
[03:32] Jordan: mmk so here's a screenshot — the 02/08 window has a series where 95th jumps at 15:12, you can see the handoff between the client and the server where the first byte is delayed by ~60ms, then tokens stream fine
[03:50] Samir: reading that, looks like the first kernel invocation is delayed. could be queueing or preemption on the GPU, or the int4 kernel has a slower init path. we should probe GPU-side SMI logs and kernel durations
[04:06] Maya: i've already captured SMI during the window; i'll attach but need permission to share more detailed traces — we'll enable a limited window of extra tracing on the VPC egress logs, shouldn't be noisy
[04:19] Marco: we can allow that for two windows, Feb 14 and Feb 15 morning windows, is that enough?
[04:26] Maya: yes that should give us a representative sample
[04:30] Jordan: also, to be clear, our prompt mix is skewed: 60% short queries (<64 tokens), 30% medium (65-512), 10% long (>2048), so any fix needs to prioritize short queries TTFT
[04:46] Samir: perfect, that means gatekeeper path for the first chunk is the right move. We'll also add a hedging policy: if first byte not returned in X ms, fallback to less-quantized kernel or an unquantized path
[05:02] Priya: hedging is fine but what's the cost delta? we have budget constraints and the product team will ask about unit cost change
[05:10] Ava: Samir, can you ballpark the cost impact of hedging to unquantized for, say, 5% of requests?
[05:18] Samir: rough numbers: if 5% fall back to fp16 path, cost increases by ~2.5% overall. if we 5% fall back to int8 it might be ~1%. We'll document exact bench numbers in the sheet
[05:30] Jordan: ok agree that 2-3% is acceptable if it stabilizes TTFT for short queries
[05:36] Ava: good. next, we talked about microburst sampling script — Samir i think you built a small tool?
[05:43] Samir: yes, it's a tiny tracer that samples request arrival and token emission timing, it outputs CSV and raw sample traces. i'll push it to a shared folder and include a README. it's lightweight, can run for an hour and produce 1k samples
[05:56] Marco: will that capture kernel-level durations or just end-to-end?
[06:00] Samir: end-to-end plus the service-side breakdown we instrument: queue wait, kernel dispatch, kernel exec, and response encode. not GPU SMI but close enough to show where the delay sits
[06:12] Priya: perfect. we'll run it against a staging endpoint, but need a replayable set of request IDs. Jordan will export them
[06:20] Jordan: yep will export by Friday
[06:23] Ava: great. any questions on the kernel fallback plan?
[06:27] Marco: one thing — for sequences >2048 you mentioned a different kernel candidate?
[06:32] Samir: yes, we have a heavy stream-optimized kernel for very long sequences that reduces per-token overhead but has larger memory working set. we will route seq>2048 to that path by default if your workload benefits from streaming, but for TTFT we prefer a small gatekeeper first-token path then switch to the long-seq kernel after a couple tokens
[06:52] Jordan: sounds complicated but ok. does this require a restart or just configuration change?
[06:56] Samir: config only. we'll push a routing rule in the canary config for 24 hours and monitor
[07:03] Maya: i'll instrument the health check to flag if the fallback rate exceeds 10% so we can rollback automatically
[07:09] Ava: nice. quick pause — any security concerns about us pulling extra traces?
[07:13] Priya: only PII redaction; we need to ensure we get read-only credentials and no payloads stored. auditing is required; SOC2 docs would help
[07:21] Ava: we'll send SOC2 summary and our retention policy right after the call.
[07:26] Jordan: thanks. also what about quantization reversal — if gatekeeper path fixes it, can we keep int4 for throughput?
[07:32] Samir: yeah the idea is hybrid: keep int4 for steady-state throughput but gatekeeper or early-token unquantized for initial latency-sensitive requests. it's a routing shim, not model retrain
[07:42] Marco: ok next, do you think changing batch thresholds could help microburst jitter?
[07:47] Samir: it might. increasing the batch wait time reduces microbatches but increases tail latency. For your short-query heavy mix we probably want aggressive small batch sizes with gatekeeper to cover first-token penalty
[08:00] Ava: let's enumerate experiments then so we can prioritize: 1) kernel gatekeeper first-token path canary 24h, 2) microburst sampling across two windows, 3) adjust batch thresholds on canary, 4) prefix cache threshold tuning. any other?
[08:16] Jordan: maybe also try a quick bench with disabled streaming to validate the streaming handshake cost
[08:20] Samir: good call, we'll include that in the bench matrix.
[08:25] Priya: timeline?
[08:27] Ava: we'll aim to have Samir's microburst script and bench sheet out today, Jordan runs sampling by 02/17, canary kernel change by 02/12, tracing windows on 02/14-15. does that work?
[08:41] Jordan: yes
[08:43] Marco: yes
[08:44] Priya: ok
[08:46] Ava: moving on, quick technical detail — Samir, you mentioned hedging thresholds. what's a reasonable X ms to trigger fallback?
[08:53] Samir: for short queries we'd start with 60ms. If first byte not observed by 60ms, trigger a parallel request to the fallback path, cancel the slower once the fast one returns. that's aggressive but keeps UX tight
[09:05] Jordan: 60ms seems ok, but if the network is the issue we might trigger too many fallbacks; that's why we want the traces
[09:12] Maya: we can add a rate limiter for hedging so it doesn't run more than 10% of requests in a sliding window
[09:18] Priya: fine, add that as a safety valve.
[09:21] Ava: perfect. Any blockers from Redwood side to push the canary?
[09:25] Samir: no blockers. I just need permission to update the canary config. Ava will coordinate with Marco to get a maintenance window
[09:33] Ava: Marco, can we have a 30-min window on Feb 12 at 10am PST for the canary flip?
[09:39] Marco: yes that works. Make sure it's low-traffic window.
[09:43] Jordan: we'll mark it in the calendar
[09:45] Ava: Great. Quick run through of deliverables: I'll send bench sheet + SOC2 + kernel config; Samir will push script; Jordan will export prompts and run microburst; Maya will enable VPC traces on 02/14-15; Marco gives maintenance window.
[10:02] Priya: any concerns about cost? we accepted a small % increase earlier but can we have an estimate in the sheet?
[10:08] Samir: will add cost delta rows for hedging to fp16 and int8 both
[10:11] Jordan: please include expected perf numbers for short, medium, long splits
[10:14] Ava: noted. Anything else?
[10:17] Marco: one last ask — can Redwood share a small runbook for rollback in case we see instability?
[10:22] Samir: yes, I'll attach a rollback runbook to the config PR
[10:26] Ava: perfect. we'll reconvene next week same time unless there are blockers; if microburst results show immediate regression we'll do an emergency deep dive. thanks everyone.
[10:36] (crosstalk) Jordan: thanks all, bye
[10:40] Ava: bye
